session_game.title: Conflict Mediation Lab
session_game.description: Mediate disputes between AI characters. Learn de-escalation, active listening, and finding win-win resolutions.

help_content.what_is: A conflict mediation simulator where you act as the mediator between two parties in dispute. AI characters represent each side with realistic emotions and positions. Learn to de-escalate, find common ground, and reach fair resolutions.
tips: Listen to both sides fully before suggesting solutions
Acknowledge emotions — people need to feel heard
Separate the person from the problem
Look for underlying interests, not just stated positions
Reframe negative statements into neutral observations

active_listening.description: Did they truly listen and acknowledge both sides?

neutrality.description: Did they remain fair and unbiased throughout?

de_escalation.description: Did they effectively calm emotions and reduce tension?

solution_quality.description: Was the proposed resolution fair and practical?

communication.description: Was their communication clear, empathetic, and professional?

process_management.description: Did they manage the conversation flow effectively?

persona_pool.name: Manish Tiwari
persona_pool.focus: being heard, getting justice, expressing frustration
persona_pool.personality: Loud and emotional. Feels wronged and wants validation. Will escalate if not acknowledged. Tests your de-escalation skills. Calms down once truly heard.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: You're clearly taking their side! Nobody is listening to me!

persona_pool.name: Sunaina Kaul
persona_pool.focus: subtle digs, indirect complaints, avoiding direct confrontation
persona_pool.personality: Appears calm but makes subtle undermining comments. Says 'it's fine' when it clearly isn't. Tests your ability to surface real issues beneath the surface.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Oh no, everything is perfectly fine. I'm sure THEY didn't mean anything by it.

persona_pool.name: Aditya Rao
persona_pool.focus: finding fair solutions, compromise, moving forward
persona_pool.personality: Calm and open to compromise. Genuinely wants resolution. But won't accept an unfair deal. Good at articulating needs. Tests if you can leverage cooperation.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I'm willing to find a middle ground, but it needs to be fair to both of us.

persona_pool.name: Lakshmi Menon
persona_pool.focus: personal hurt, trust betrayal, emotional validation
persona_pool.personality: Deeply hurt on a personal level. This isn't just about the issue — it's about broken trust. Needs emotional validation before they can discuss solutions. May cry or get very quiet.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: It's not about the work. It's that I trusted them and they let me down.

persona_pool.name: Rajesh Singhania
persona_pool.personality: Senior person who uses their position as leverage. Expects special treatment. Dismisses the other party's concerns. Tests if you can handle power imbalance in mediation.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I've been here 15 years. You expect me to apologize to someone who joined last month?

persona_pool.name: Dr. Namrata Joshi
persona_pool.personality: Keeps detailed records. Every claim is backed by emails, screenshots, or policy documents. Tests if you can work with objective evidence and not just emotions.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I have the email chain right here. On March 3rd, they committed to...

persona_pool.name: Sanjay Dwivedi
persona_pool.focus: being wronged, unfairness, seeking sympathy, avoiding responsibility
persona_pool.personality: Sees themselves as the victim in every situation. Avoids taking responsibility for their part. Seeks sympathy rather than solutions. Tests your ability to gently push toward accountability.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: This always happens to me. Everyone takes advantage of my good nature.

persona_pool.name: Nandini Chakraborty
persona_pool.focus: moving forward, practical solutions, time efficiency
persona_pool.personality: Pragmatic and forward-looking. Less interested in rehashing the past, more interested in fixing the future. May be impatient with emotional processing. Tests balanced mediation.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Can we skip the blame game and figure out what we're actually going to do?

scenarios.title: Roommate Conflict — Living Together
scenarios.description: Two roommates are at each other's throats. Cleanliness, noise, shared expenses — small issues have snowballed into major tension. You're their mutual friend asked to help.
scenarios.setting: Your apartment's living room. Both roommates sit on opposite ends of the sofa, arms crossed, not making eye contact.
scenarios.session_topic: Mediating a conflict between two roommates about shared living responsibilities
coaching_tips: Let each person share without interruption
Focus on future behavior, not past blame

storybook_pages.title: The Tension
storybook_pages.text: Your two friends have been roommates for 6 months. What started as small annoyances — dirty dishes, loud music, unpaid bills — has become a cold war. They've asked you to help.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Two Indian roommates sitting apart in a messy apartment living room, arms crossed, tense atmosphere, mutual friend arriving, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Both Sides
storybook_pages.text: You've heard whispered complaints from both sides. Each thinks the other is the problem. Neither has tried to have a real conversation. That's where you come in.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Split scene showing each Indian roommate separately complaining to their friend, speech bubbles with frustrations, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Conversation
storybook_pages.text: They're both here. The air is thick with tension. You take a deep breath. 'Okay, let's talk about this. One at a time. Who wants to start?'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Three Indian friends in living room, mediator in middle seat, both parties on sides, about to start conversation, warm but tense, digital art

scenarios.title: Team Dispute — Credit & Blame
scenarios.description: Two team members are in a heated dispute over project credit. One feels their work was stolen; the other says they did most of the work. You're the team lead.
scenarios.setting: A small meeting room. You've called both team members in after their argument disrupted the team standup.
scenarios.session_topic: Resolving a team dispute about project ownership and credit
coaching_tips: Ask for specific examples from both sides
Separate the credit issue from the working relationship

storybook_pages.title: The Blowup
storybook_pages.text: It happened in the middle of the team standup. Manish said 'MY project delivered great results.' Lakshmi snapped: 'YOUR project? I did 80% of the work!' The team went silent.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian office standup meeting, two colleagues arguing while team watches uncomfortably, open office space, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Team Lead's Call
storybook_pages.text: As team lead, this is your problem now. Both are talented. Losing either would hurt the team. But the tension is affecting everyone's work.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian team lead at desk thinking, two angry employee photos on screen, HR escalation email visible, concerned expression, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Meeting
storybook_pages.text: You've booked a private room. Both arrive, still fuming. 'I've asked you both here because we need to resolve this. The team can't function like this.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Small meeting room, Indian team lead between two upset colleagues, door closed, private mediation beginning, digital art

scenarios.title: Family Business — Succession Dispute
scenarios.description: Two siblings are fighting over the family business direction. One wants to modernize, the other wants to preserve traditions. You're a family friend called in to mediate.
scenarios.setting: The family's ancestral home in Jaipur. Family photos line the walls. The weight of three generations hangs in the air.
scenarios.session_topic: Mediating a succession and direction dispute between siblings in a family business
coaching_tips: Find solutions that honor both tradition and innovation
learning_objectives: Navigate emotional and business stakes simultaneously

storybook_pages.title: Three Generations
storybook_pages.text: The Singhania textile business has been running for 70 years. Their grandfather started it, their father grew it. Now two siblings must decide its future — and they can't agree.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Beautiful ancestral Indian haveli in Jaipur with textile factory in background, family photo frames on wall showing three generations, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Two Visions
storybook_pages.text: Rajesh wants to go digital — e-commerce, AI-driven inventory, international expansion. His sister wants to preserve the craftsmanship, the workers, the legacy. Both have valid points.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Split scene - modern digital warehouse on one side, traditional Indian textile workshop with artisans on other, two siblings, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Family Friend
storybook_pages.text: You've known both since childhood. Their parents trusted you. 'Please help us figure this out before it tears the family apart.' The weight of generations rests on this conversation.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian family meeting in ancestral home drawing room, mediator friend arriving, two siblings waiting, emotional atmosphere, digital art

scenarios.title: Student vs. Faculty — Academic Conflict
scenarios.description: A student is accusing a professor of unfair grading. The professor insists the grade is justified. You're the department head mediating.
scenarios.setting: The department head's office in a university. Books line the walls. Both parties sit across from you.
scenarios.session_topic: Resolving a grading dispute between a student and professor

storybook_pages.title: The Complaint
storybook_pages.text: A student walks into your office with tears in their eyes: 'Sir, I worked for three months on that project. Dr. Joshi gave me a C. My classmate who copied half my approach got a B+.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian university student in professor's office, upset, showing assignment papers, book-lined walls, academic setting, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Other Side
storybook_pages.text: Dr. Joshi is firm: 'I've been teaching 20 years. The student's work had fundamental errors. I don't grade on effort alone.' Both believe they're right.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian professor at desk defending grading decision, grade sheets visible, academic office, firm but professional expression, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Decision
storybook_pages.text: As department head, you must find a resolution. The student's career could be affected. The professor's authority must be respected. Both sit before you, waiting.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian department head behind desk, student on one side, professor on other, university office, mediation about to begin, digital art

scenarios.title: Neighbor Dispute — The Parking War
scenarios.description: Two neighbors are in an escalating dispute over a parking spot. What started as an inconvenience has turned into a feud. The RWA president (you) must mediate.
scenarios.setting: The community hall of an apartment complex. Two neighbors sit on opposite sides of a table, clearly unhappy to be here.
scenarios.session_topic: Mediating a parking dispute between apartment neighbors
coaching_tips: Focus on practical solutions, not who was 'right'
learning_objectives: Find practical solutions for everyday disputes

storybook_pages.title: The Parking War
storybook_pages.text: What started as one car parked in the wrong spot has escalated into blocked driveways, angry notes, and now a formal complaint. As RWA president, you must step in.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian apartment complex parking lot, two cars blocking each other, angry notes on windshields, frustrated residents, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Taking Sides
storybook_pages.text: Other residents are taking sides. WhatsApp groups are buzzing. If this isn't resolved soon, a simple parking issue could split the entire community.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian apartment residents in groups discussing, WhatsApp messages on phones, community hall in background, taking sides, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Mediation
storybook_pages.text: Both neighbors arrive at the community hall. Neither wants to be here. 'Okay, let's discuss this like adults. This is our community, and we have to live together.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian apartment community hall, RWA president mediating between two neighbors, simple meeting table, residential building visible through window, digital art

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

title: Conflict Mediation
description: Take the seat of a neutral mediator between two colleagues in dispute. Practice active listening, impartial framing, and de-escalation to reach a resolution that works for everyone.
coaching_moment: Take the seat of a neutral mediator between two colleagues in dispute. Practice active listening, impartial framing, and de-escalation to reach a resolution that works for everyone.
cultural_context: India's diverse society — with its caste, religious, regional, and linguistic dimensions — creates rich contexts for conflict and equally rich opportunities for mediation. Conflict resolution skills support both professional effectiveness and social cohesion.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through negotiation gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Where did you give ground, and where did you hold it? What did the other side teach you about your own priorities?
